rendered: The text says that L- and D-HGNRs both show mirror-image CD responses, with two distinct chiroptical peaks at 585 nm and 790 nm[1] (Fig. 1[2]c). Because the spectra are mirror images, the D-HGNRs have the opposite sign to the L-HGNRs at each peak. A vision model's reading of the plot (an estimate, not printed text) gives the D-HGNRs a positive peak near the shorter wavelength and a negative band near the longer wavelength, with slightly different positions:[3][4] positive peak of about 370 mdeg near 592 nm[5] and negative band of about −255 mdeg near 830 nm[6].
